clue.text: Get angry and quickly get away from other middle name

parts.note: to fly off is to leave in a hurry

indicators.note: the word other loses its outer letters, keeping only its central run

parts.note: a handle is slang for a person's name or title

explanation.surface: Someone flees in a temper on hearing an unusual middle name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle' takes OTHER without its ends, giving THE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to lose one's temper suddenly, like an axe head flying loose.

clue.text: Mass departures from previous mix of uniform doses

parts.note: ex- is a prefix meaning former or previous

indicators.note: a mix stirs these letters into a fresh order

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: People leaving after an earlier blend of standard medicine doses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix of' rearranges U and DOSES into ODUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a biblical word for a large-scale going-out of people, as from Egypt.

clue.text: Jenny used to be in the navy

definitions.meaning: jenny is a traditional pet name for a small brown songbird

definitions.text: used to be in the navy
definitions.meaning: a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service, the former British navy branch for women

explanation.surface: A woman named Jenny once served at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenny wren is the folk name for the bird; Wrens were women in Britain's navy until 1993.

clue.text: Go over what we all do in 8 down

definitions.meaning: to topple or tumble to the ground

definitions.text: what we all do in 8 down

explanation.surface: A reference to the rhyme's collapsing finale.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple is to drop to the ground; the rhyme's last line has everyone do it.

clue.text: Lightweight dressing gown

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight
a robe is a loose gown worn over nightclothes

explanation.surface: A flimsy, featherlight bathrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightweight' must be split into 'Light' (the definition) and 'weight' (ST, for stone, 14 pounds).
explanation.definitionFit: A flashing lamp used in discos and photography is a kind of lamp or illumination.

clue.text: Prison officer, I heard, is a supporter of hanging

parts.note: screw is British slang for a prison warder

indicators.note: the speaker's word I is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE

explanation.surface: A jailer confesses to favouring capital punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a supporter of hanging' suggests the gallows, but it means something that holds up a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded ring screwed into wood, used to suspend pictures, mirrors and similar items.

clue.text: He draws a regular tidy income subbing Times leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: A man earns a neat steady wage by standing in for the editors of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leaders' looks like newspaper editorials; 'leaders' applies to all six preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sketches or paints pictures is a painter or illustrator.

clue.text: Gruesome song with rare origins

indicators.note: gruesome suggests something mangled, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grisly nursery tune whose beginnings are obscure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gruesome' shuffles SONG and RARE ORIGINS. The rhyme is popularly, though doubtfully, linked to the plague, hence both gruesome and of uncertain origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's ring-dance rhyme, folk-linked to plague symptoms, whose real beginnings are unknown.

clue.text: Sumptuous place on the Nile needs nothing altered before one starts to advertise new tenancy

indicators.note: the round letter standing for nothing is changed to another vowel

parts.note: Luxor is an Egyptian city on the Nile
O looks like zero, nothing
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the starts are the first letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: An upmarket Egyptian property for rent needs no changes before advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing altered' turns LUXOR's O into U, giving LUXUR; 'starts to' picks ANT from 'advertise new tenancy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxuriant means lush and rich in abundance, close to lavish or opulent.

clue.text: Gas safety body once favoured by the Queen?

definitions.meaning: the Council for Registered Gas Installers, the former UK gas safety register
Elizabeth II famously kept Welsh short-legged dogs of this breed

explanation.surface: A former regulator enjoying royal approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym of the old gas register matches the dog breed beloved of Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Ordain reuse of Latin service book

indicators.note: reusing the word's letters means putting them to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to ordain a priest using the old Latin rite book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reuse of' rearranges ORDAIN into ORDINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A book setting out the forms of a church office, such as ordination, is a liturgical manual.

clue.text: Opportunity to get round writer with gin cocktail

parts.note: O is round in shape
a pen is a writing implement

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A chance to win over an author with a gin drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance or opening is a favourable moment to act, a synonym of chance.

clue.text: Rubbish mostly run together

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its first two letters being dropped

parts.note: refuse is waste or garbage

explanation.surface: Junk largely melts into one mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' here drops the front RE rather than the usual last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To melt or join into a single mass is to merge or blend.

clue.text: Private correspondence means nothing to the landlord

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring
one who lets property is a letter

explanation.surface: Personal mail is of no concern to the property owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the landlord' is one who lets, a setter's favourite trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic note between sweethearts is intimate personal mail.

clue.text: One who used to be known for keeping insect close to extinction

definitions.text: One who used to be known

parts.note: to keep something is to have it
a bee is an insect

indicators.note: the close of the word extinction is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone famous for preserving an endangered insect species.
explanation.definitionFit: A faded celebrity is someone whose fame or success lies in the past.

clue.text: Fertilised hen cried out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A hen squawked when her egg was fertilised.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil treated with manure or nutrients has been made richer.

clue.text: Test out issue for the head

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: A doctor checks a matter concerning the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TEST into STET.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed cowboy hat is something worn on the head.

clue.text: Friendly Society getting one capable of doing things

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
able means competent to act

explanation.surface: A friendly society recruits a competent member.
explanation.walkthrough: A friendly society is a British mutual aid association, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sociable enjoys company and is affable and gregarious.

clue.text: Quiet sex appeal gets hospital series to become a great success

indicators.note: gets here means takes in or receives, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
M*A*S*H was a US television series set in an army field hospital
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A subdued sexy medical drama becomes a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: M*A*S*H was a long-running US sitcom about a Korean War field hospital; the outer pair spells a rude word, part of the setter's mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway hit record or show is a huge popular triumph.

clue.text: Revised format of speech therapy, missing the extra dimension

indicators.note: a revised format puts these letters into a new arrangement
missing says certain letters are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A rewritten speech therapy course lacks an additional component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised format of' shuffles SPEECH THERAPY, and 'missing' takes out the letters of THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction's fourth-dimensional realm allowing faster-than-light travel beyond ordinary space.

clue.text: 8 down said to be about this in London, where capital is changing hands

definitions.text: 8 down said to be about this in London

indicators.note: right is swapped for left, R becoming L

parts.note: Prague is the Czech capital

explanation.surface: The rhyme supposedly describes the Great Plague of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' turns R (right) into L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme is traditionally, if doubtfully, said to describe the Great Plague of 1665.

clue.text: Flowers about one's person in 8 down

definitions.meaning: the rhyme has 'a pocket full of' them, carried about one's person

explanation.surface: Blooms carried in the pockets in the rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bouquets of blooms; the rhyme's pocket full of them were said to ward off disease.

clue.text: Even in thralldom there is glory

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters, second, fourth and so on, are taken from the word

explanation.surface: Even in bondage there is honour to be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of light round a saint's head, or a glow of renown, is a radiance or glory.

clue.text: New to the audience, dances lead off with small changes

indicators.note: said to listeners, the word new is spelt as it is pronounced

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like NU

indicators.note: the leading letter of dances is removed

explanation.surface: Fresh steps shown to spectators, with minor alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: NU is the Greek letter, which is pronounced like 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtle shades of meaning or slight variations are fine distinctions.

clue.text: Overheard a complete fabrication twice over in 8 down

indicators.note: overheard means the phrase is taken as heard, not as written

parts.note: a tissue of lies is a complete fabrication

explanation.surface: An eavesdropped total lie, repeated, in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme's line is 'A-tishoo! A-tishoo!', a sneeze said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The sneeze appears doubled in the rhyme just before everyone falls down.

clue.text: Very small particles found in a television set

indicators.note: the letters are found within the run of words a television set

explanation.surface: Tiny particles discovered inside a TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Charged atoms or molecules are tiny bits of matter.

clue.text: It magnifies differences for couple starting off

indicators.note: differences suggest the letters are changed into a new order
the starting letter of couple is taken off

explanation.surface: Something exaggerates rifts between partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting off' drops C from COUPLE; 'differences for' rearranges OUPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeweller's small magnifying glass is held to the eye to enlarge detail.

clue.text: This flower is not inelegant

indicators.note: not says the word as printed is not the arrangement wanted, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Praise for a flower's grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not inelegant' reads as praise, but 'not' signals that INELEGANT is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the sweetbriar, a wild rose bloom.
